report.summary: Reviewed chunk 5 of 5 of cancel.py: defines ManagedProcess properties, cancel, close, and context manager methods.
risks: cancel method | medium | Uses hardcoded 10s timeout in kill_tree wait; if container kill hangs, could block. | Check if timeout is configurable or if alternative fallback exists.
close method | low | Returns None if already released, but return type is CancelResult | None; caller may not expect None. | Verify callers handle None.
__del__ method | low | Calls close with grace_s=0.0; if close raises, exception is silently caught. | Consider logging or different handling.

handoff.purpose: Properties, cancel, close, context manager, and destructor for ManagedProcess.

claims.text: Idempotent: cancelling an already-exited process is a no-op that reports ``already_exited``.
claims.why: Lines 506-508: if self._process.poll() is not None, returns CancelResult with STAGE_ALREADY_EXITED.

claims.text: Stop the tree, escalating from a group signal to a container kill.
claims.why: Lines 510-534: first signal_group, then if process still running, kill_tree.

claims.text: Cancel if still running, then release the container. Idempotent.
claims.why: Lines 537-548: if not released, cancels if process alive, then releases; if already released, returns None.

claims.text: The underlying ``Popen`` (for stdio); do not signal it directly.
claims.why: Returns self._process; comment warns not to signal directly.
